summary: Backend-only regression + new MarketingSettings.timezone field testing. All 18 prior marketing tests pass, all 15 prior push tests pass, and 4 new timezone tests pass — total 37/37. Default GET returns 'timezone':'UTC'; valid IANA tz ('America/Phoenix') persists round-trip; >64 char tz returns 422; invalid tz string ('Not/Real_TZ') is accepted by the model (no IANA validation enforced — by design) and does NOT crash adjacent endpoints — /api/admin/push/send-test still returned 200 with clean JSON. Backend logs confirm '[push] daily-reminder scheduler started' on startup and zero '_send_daily_reminder error' lines were observed during the run, validating the zoneinfo→UTC fallback path.
critical_code_review_comments: MarketingSettings.timezone has no IANA validation — invalid strings like 'Not/Real_TZ' silently persist. The scheduler safely falls back to UTC, but if you want stricter UX, validate against zoneinfo.available_timezones() in a Pydantic field_validator (or, at minimum, log a warning at save time so admins notice the typo).

server.py is now ~3670 lines. Marketing/Push/Scheduler logic should be split into routers/services modules (admin, marketing, push, jobs) for maintainability — already flagged in iter 9, no progress yet.
MarketingSettings.dict() is deprecated in Pydantic v2 (server.py L3407, L3423, L3426) — prefer .model_dump(). Same note applies to PushSubscriptionKeys.dict() (already flagged iter 9).

The scheduler stores tz_name in push_reminder_log but the idempotency key (date) is derived from now_local in the saved tz; if an admin changes timezone mid-day, the same calendar date in the new tz could re-trigger a send. Low-risk, but worth a comment.

save_marketing_settings does a full $set of every field — there is no patch/merge endpoint, so any partial-update client must always send the full document (already required because of Pydantic's MarketingSettings schema). Acceptable, just document for FE.
